messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Pager: KV cache amplification detected for continuous-batching on MQA routes (mistral-v3 / qwen-7b). Latency > 2.5s P95 for 2m, errors (429/503) rising. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-contbatch
alex: I’m oncall. looking at graphs now. can someone post the hot paths?
priya: hitting this too, saw export showing big spike in prefix cardinality on shard-12 and a sudden prefetch multiplier increase.
ming: logs show repeated cache misses + concurrent continuous-batch spikes. looks like split-shard prefetch policy started duplicating requests across node groups.
carlos: timeline: at 14:01 UTC we deployed a small change to prefetch heuristics (split-shard aware). metrics were fine in staging. in prod at 14:16 latency climbed.
leah: customer impact? any premium tenants affected?
alex: a handful of Dedicated customers saw >50% token latency increase, billing unaffected but streaming timeouts hit. some clients retried which amplified load.
priya: quick snapshot of error rates: 14:10 -> 14:20 : 429s went from 0.2% to 8.6%, 503s from 0% to 1.3% (per-route mqa/mistral-v3).
ming: raw tail sample from shard-12: ```
2025-11-03T14:18:02Z ERROR cache.go:421 miss: prefix-card 124k, inflight=32, cont-batch-size=128
2025-11-03T14:18:02Z WARN batcher.go:87 duplicate-prefetch triggered for key=abc123
```
carlos: rolling back the heuristic might be the fastest mitigation, but we should also consider throttling continuous-batching for suspicious prefixes.
alex: agree. plan: 1) toggle prefetch split-shard flag off 2) set cont-batch max to 32 on MQA routes 3) scale replica pool for shard-12 by +2. executing now — will coordinate with infra.
priya: toggle command: `POST /admin/flags/split_shard_prefetch false` (internal flag). I can run it in 30s.
ming: while toggling, add temporary prefix-cardinality guard: `prefetch.max_prefix=5000` on route config.
leah: I’ll notify CSMs: potentially impacted accounts list attached. preparing customer note: ETA 10-15m.
alex: executing flag toggle now. 
IncidentBot: DeployBot: flag toggle request received by infra-api (req id: r-9b3).
priya: toggle succeeded. seeing prefetch queue dropping in 1m.
ming: setting cont-batch max: `cfg set /routes/mqa/cont_batch_max 32 --env prod` -> applied.
carlos: scaling shard-12: `k scale deployment kv-shard-12 --replicas=6` -> in progress.
alex: early signals: P95 down from 2.6s -> 1.1s within 3m. 429s trending back to baseline. good.
leah: sending customer update: "We've applied mitigations to reduce latency and risk of timeouts. We're continuing to monitor and will follow up with a detailed postmortem." cc: @account-team.
priya: quick post-action check: KV eviction counts jumped; we might have thrashed small-value prefixes — add to follow-up.
ming: note for postmortem: root cause hypothesis: split-shard prefetch multiplied prefetch targets for high-cardinality prefixes (MQA), causing cache blowup + cont-batcher amplification. fallback model variants (qwen-variant-lowprefetch) didn't engage because routing policy pinned to mistral-v3.
carlos: interesting edge: GQA routes appear unaffected — they short-circuit prefetch for large-card prefixes. config divergence between GQA/MQA was a factor.
alex: next steps (short): 1) keep split_shard_prefetch off 2) keep cont_batch_max lower for MQA for 24h 3) run prefix-cardinality scan to identify hot keys 4) restore capacity and soft-limit prefetch for high-card prefixes 5) schedule postmortem and regression test.
leah: customer impact summary for ops report: Affected: 5 Dedicated customers (latency spikes, retry loops), ~0.4% overall API error rate bump for 12m window, no data exfiltration, no billing anomalies.
IncidentBot: PagerDuty: oncall-ops acknowledged the incident.
oncall-ops: I’ll take handoff for postmortem and customer follow-up. please add investigation notes to the incident board: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2750012345
priya: adding logs + perf dump to thread. also adding the CLI commands we ran for reproducibility: ```
# toggle
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://infra-api/flags/split_shard_prefetch -d '{"value":false}'
# set cont batch max
redwoodctl config set /routes/mqa/cont_batch_max 32 --env prod
# scale
kubectl -n inference scale deployment/kv-shard-12 --replicas=6
```
ming: postmortem questions: - why didn't canary catch this? - how did retry amplification interplay with client SDK backoff? - do we need a prefetch circuit-breaker?
carlos: on canary: the config change only ran in staging with a small synthetic workload; staging didn't mimic prefix-cardinality of production customers. we need a canary with high-prefix-card workloads.
ale x: (typo) alex: i can own the canary test creation. will pair with research to build high-card load generator.
leah: closing notes: will draft exec summary after postmortem. tagging @sre-bot to create incident ticket and link runbook.
sre-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2025-1123. Linked runbook: kv-contbatch. Assigned to oncall-ops.
oncall-ops: taking ownership. will follow up with timeline, RCA draft, and customer outreach plan. thanks all for speedy mitigation. :thumbsup:
priya: quick addendum: we should consider a default prefetch cap for any route where prefix-cardinality > 10k. adding to backlog.
ming: logging note: add metric `prefetch.duplicates` and an alert when duplicates > 50/min per shard.
carlos: adding it to eng-infra backlog and will PR a config change tomorrow.
alex: thanks team. I’m marking this thread resolved for the immediate pager. leaving the ticket open for postmortem work.
IncidentBot: Incident resolved (mitigation applied). Time to P0 -> P1: 00:17:35.
